Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For every $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$, with $\Gamma$ as in [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]], there is a unique $u=S\lambda\in\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ satisfying the weak single-layer equation of [[def-bem-laplace-layer-potentials-and-energy-spaces]]. It is harmonic on $\Omega^-$ and $\Omega^+$, its two traces agree, and its weak conormal traces satisfy
$$\partial_n^-u-\partial_n^+u=\lambda\quad\hbox{in }H^{-1/2}(\Gamma).$$
The trace operator $V\lambda:=\gamma u$ maps $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ boundedly into $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, and there are constants $C,c>0$ depending on $\Gamma$ such that
$$\|u\|_{\dot H^1}+\|V\lambda\|_{H^{1/2}}\le C\|\lambda\|_{H^{-1/2}},\qquad \langle\lambda,V\lambda\rangle_\Gamma\ge c\|\lambda\|_{H^{-1/2}}^2.$$
If $\lambda\in L^\infty(\Gamma)$ (in particular for facewise smooth densities reaching edges or discontinuous P0 densities), this weak potential agrees away from $\Gamma$ with $\int_\Gamma(4\pi|x-y|)^{-1}\lambda(y)dS_y$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For every $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, the affine class $\mathcal A_\phi$ in [[def-bem-double-layer-transmission-space]] has a unique minimum-energy pair $D\phi=(u^-,u^+)$. It is harmonic on both sides, satisfies
$$\gamma^-D\phi-\gamma^+D\phi=-\phi,\qquad \partial_n^-D\phi=\partial_n^+D\phi,$$
and obeys
$$\|\nabla u^-\|_{L^2(\Omega^-)}+\|\nabla u^+\|_{L^2(\Omega^+)}\le C\|\phi\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}.$$
Consequently the average trace $K\phi=(\gamma^-D\phi+\gamma^+D\phi)/2$ is in $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ and the common conormal $q_\phi=\partial_n^-D\phi=\partial_n^+D\phi$ is in $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$, with both maps bounded. For every $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, the weak potential agrees away from $\Gamma$, with smooth representatives, with the absolutely convergent integral $\int_\Gamma\partial_{n_y}G_3(x,y)\phi(y)dS_y$. No vanishing condition at polyhedral edges or vertices is required.

For $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ define the Laplace Calderon boundary operators by
$$V\lambda=\gamma S\lambda,\qquad K\phi=\tfrac12(\gamma^-D\phi+\gamma^+D\phi),$$
$$K'\lambda=\tfrac12(\partial_n^-S\lambda+\partial_n^+S\lambda),\qquad W\phi=-\partial_n^-D\phi=-\partial_n^+D\phi.$$
Here $\gamma S\lambda$ is the common trace, conormal traces use the orientation of [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]], and the last equality is meaningful because the weak double layer has a common conormal derivative. This page uses the real duality pairing between $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$. The well-definedness and bounded mapping properties of $V,K,K',W$ are proved in [[thm-bem-calderon-mapping-and-jump-identities]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice and let $\Gamma$ be any compact Lipschitz boundary in the geometry of [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]]; no polyhedral restriction is imposed. The interior trace $\gamma^-:H^1(\Omega^-)\to H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ is bounded. On every bounded exterior boundary collar $C=\Omega^+\cap U$, where $U$ is a bounded neighborhood of $\Gamma$ with Lipschitz collar boundary, the exterior trace $\gamma^+:H^1(C)\to H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ is bounded. The corresponding localized assertion holds over each boundary chart. Thus an exterior function has this trace whenever it is $H^1$ up to the boundary on such collars; membership in $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega^+)$ alone does not assert a boundary trace. There is a bounded linear right inverse $L:H^{1/2}(\Gamma)\to H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ with $\gamma(Lg)=g$. There is also a bounded extension operator $E:H^1(\Omega^-)\to H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ with $(Eu)|_{\Omega^-}=u$.

Let $\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ denote the completion of $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ in the norm $\|u\|_{\dot H^1}=\|\nabla u\|_{L^2}$. Its elements have an $L^6$ representative, the trace $\gamma:\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)\to H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ is bounded, and the right inverse above may be chosen with compact support near $\Gamma$.

routine_steps.claim: The bounds for $V$ and $K$ are respectively the trace bound in [F1] and the average-trace bound in [F2]. The bound for $W$ is the common-conormal bound in [F2] and the definition in [F3]. For $K'$, harmonicity of $S\lambda$ and the weak conormal definition give, for every $g\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, $|\langle\partial_n^-S\lambda,g\rangle|\le\|\nabla S\lambda\|_{L^2(\Omega^-)}\|\nabla L^-g\|_{L^2(\Omega^-)}\le C\|\lambda\|_{H^{-1/2}}\|g\|_{H^{1/2}},$ and the exterior estimate is identical with an exterior local lift. Thus both conormals, and their average $K'\lambda$, lie in $H^{-1/2}$ with the claimed bound.

The first common-trace identity and the single-layer conormal difference are [F1]. By [F3], $K'\lambda$ is the arithmetic mean of those two conormals; solving the sum-and-difference equations gives the displayed $K'\pm\tfrac12 I$ formulas. The double-layer jump and average-trace definition [F2]–[F3] similarly give $K\mp\tfrac12 I$ for the interior/exterior traces. The common double-layer conormal equals $-W\phi$ by [F3]. These algebraic identities establish every signed formula.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Gamma$ be as above, let $\mathcal T_h$ be any finite conforming surface triangulation, and let $X_h$ be its P0 space. For every $f\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ there are unique $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $\lambda_h\in X_h$ satisfying
$$\langle\mu,V\lambda\rangle_\Gamma=\langle\mu,f\rangle_\Gamma\quad(\mu\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)),\qquad \langle\mu_h,V\lambda_h\rangle_\Gamma=\langle\mu_h,f\rangle_\Gamma\quad(\mu_h\in X_h).$$
For constants $c,C>0$ from [[thm-bem-single-layer-transmission-mapping-and-coercivity]],
$$\|\lambda-\lambda_h\|_{H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)}\le(1+C/c)\inf_{\mu_h\in X_h}\|\lambda-\mu_h\|_{H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)}.$$
The method is conforming because $X_h\subset H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$; this is an exact Galerkin estimate and contains no quadrature or geometry error.

Let $\{\mathcal T_h\}$ be a shape-regular family of conforming surface triangulations of $\Gamma$ from [[def-bem-surface-mesh-and-piecewise-constant-density-space]], and let $h=\max_{T\in\mathcal T_h}h_T$. For $v\in L^1(\Gamma)$ define the element-average projection
$$\Pi_hv|_T=|T|^{-1}\int_Tv\,ds.$$
There is a family-independent constant $C$ such that
$$\|v-\Pi_hv\|_{L^2(\Gamma)}\le Ch^{1/2}\|v\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}\qquad(v\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)).$$
If $\lambda$ is continuously differentiable on each planar face (with facewise derivatives square integrable), then
$$\|\lambda-\Pi_h\lambda\|_{H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)}\le Ch^{3/2}\|\nabla_\Gamma\lambda\|_{L^2(\Gamma)}.$$
Here $\nabla_\Gamma\lambda$ is the ordinary two-dimensional gradient on each planar face; no continuity of these derivatives across edges is assumed.

derivations.claim: In [F1], choose the admissible comparison density $\mu_h=\Pi_h\lambda\in X_h$. Then the best-approximation infimum is at most $\|\lambda-\Pi_h\lambda\|_{H^{-1/2}}$.
Apply [F2] to the right-hand side of step 1.1 and absorb the mesh-independent quasi-optimality factor into $C$. This gives the displayed $h^{3/2}$ estimate.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For every $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, the affine class $\mathcal A_\phi$ in [[def-bem-double-layer-transmission-space]] has a unique minimum-energy pair $D\phi=(u^-,u^+)$. It is harmonic on both sides, satisfies
$$\gamma^-D\phi-\gamma^+D\phi=-\phi,\qquad \partial_n^-D\phi=\partial_n^+D\phi,$$
and obeys
$$\|\nabla u^-\|_{L^2(\Omega^-)}+\|\nabla u^+\|_{L^2(\Omega^+)}\le C\|\phi\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}.$$
Consequently the average trace $K\phi=(\gamma^-D\phi+\gamma^+D\phi)/2$ is in $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ and the common conormal $q_\phi=\partial_n^-D\phi=\partial_n^+D\phi$ is in $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$, with both maps bounded. For every $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, the weak potential agrees away from $\Gamma$, with smooth representatives, with the absolutely convergent integral $\int_\Gamma\partial_{n_y}G_3(x,y)\phi(y)dS_y$. No vanishing condition at polyhedral edges or vertices is required.

For $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ define the Laplace Calderon boundary operators by
$$V\lambda=\gamma S\lambda,\qquad K\phi=\tfrac12(\gamma^-D\phi+\gamma^+D\phi),$$
$$K'\lambda=\tfrac12(\partial_n^-S\lambda+\partial_n^+S\lambda),\qquad W\phi=-\partial_n^-D\phi=-\partial_n^+D\phi.$$
Here $\gamma S\lambda$ is the common trace, conormal traces use the orientation of [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]], and the last equality is meaningful because the weak double layer has a common conormal derivative. This page uses the real duality pairing between $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$. The well-definedness and bounded mapping properties of $V,K,K',W$ are proved in [[thm-bem-calderon-mapping-and-jump-identities]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice, as in the single- and double-layer transmission theorems. For $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, the operators in [[def-bem-calderon-boundary-operators]] are bounded as
$$V:H^{-1/2}\to H^{1/2},\quad K:H^{1/2}\to H^{1/2},\quad K':H^{-1/2}\to H^{-1/2},\quad W:H^{1/2}\to H^{-1/2}.$$
Their weak traces satisfy
$$\gamma^-S\lambda=\gamma^+S\lambda=V\lambda,\qquad \partial_n^-S\lambda=K'\lambda+\tfrac12\lambda,\quad \partial_n^+S\lambda=K'\lambda-\tfrac12\lambda,$$
$$\gamma^-D\phi=K\phi-\tfrac12\phi,\qquad \gamma^+D\phi=K\phi+\tfrac12\phi,\qquad \partial_n^-D\phi=\partial_n^+D\phi=-W\phi.$$
All equalities are in the stated Sobolev trace or dual spaces and use the outward normal orientation fixed on the A page.

nonempty bounded connected extension domain, and let $1\le p<\infty$. Then there is
$C=C(\Omega,p)$ such that every $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ satisfies
$$\|u-u_\Omega\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)},\qquad u_\Omega:=|\Omega|^{-1}\int_\Omega u(x)\,dx.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice and let $\Gamma$ be any compact Lipschitz boundary in the geometry of [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]]; no polyhedral restriction is imposed. The interior trace $\gamma^-:H^1(\Omega^-)\to H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ is bounded. On every bounded exterior boundary collar $C=\Omega^+\cap U$, where $U$ is a bounded neighborhood of $\Gamma$ with Lipschitz collar boundary, the exterior trace $\gamma^+:H^1(C)\to H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ is bounded. The corresponding localized assertion holds over each boundary chart. Thus an exterior function has this trace whenever it is $H^1$ up to the boundary on such collars; membership in $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega^+)$ alone does not assert a boundary trace. There is a bounded linear right inverse $L:H^{1/2}(\Gamma)\to H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ with $\gamma(Lg)=g$. There is also a bounded extension operator $E:H^1(\Omega^-)\to H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ with $(Eu)|_{\Omega^-}=u$.

Let $\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ denote the completion of $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ in the norm $\|u\|_{\dot H^1}=\|\nabla u\|_{L^2}$. Its elements have an $L^6$ representative, the trace $\gamma:\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)\to H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ is bounded, and the right inverse above may be chosen with compact support near $\Gamma$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For the connected exterior domain $\Omega^+$ of [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]], let
$$E^+(\Omega^+)=\{u\in H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega^+):u\in L^6(\Omega^+),\ \nabla u\in L^2(\Omega^+)\}.$$
There is a constant $C$ depending only on $\Omega^-$ and its fixed trace atlas such that every $u\in E^+(\Omega^+)$ has $\gamma^+u\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ and
$$\|\gamma^+u\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}\le C\|\nabla u\|_{L^2(\Omega^+)}.$$

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, let $a$ be a bounded coercive sesquilinear form on $H$ with constants $M,\alpha$ ([[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]]), and let $F:H\to\mathbb K$ be a bounded conjugate-linear functional with norm $\|F\|=\sup_{\|v\|\le1}|F(v)|$. The real bilinear case is the same statement with $a$ symmetric or not, $F$ a bounded linear functional, and the conjugation read as the identity.

derivations.claim: Put $\bar\phi=|\Gamma|^{-1}m_\Gamma(\phi)$ and $\phi_0=\phi-\bar\phi$. The quotient norm controls $\|\phi_0\|_{H^{1/2}}$: for any constant $a$, the $L^2$ bound gives $|\bar\phi-a|\le |\Gamma|^{-1/2}\|\phi-a\|_{L^2}$, hence $\|\phi_0\|_{H^{1/2}}\le C\|\phi-a\|_{H^{1/2}}$, and take the infimum. Also $|\bar\phi|=|m_\Gamma(\phi)|/|\Gamma|$. Thus $\|\phi\|_{H^{1/2}}^2\le C(\inf_a\|\phi-a\|_{H^{1/2}}^2+|m_\Gamma(\phi)|^2)$. By [F2], $W$ is bounded; the rank-one term is bounded because $|m_\Gamma(\phi)|\le|\Gamma|^{1/2}\|\phi\|_{L^2}\le C\|\phi\|_{H^{1/2}}$, so $b$ is bounded. Its coercivity follows from step 2.1 and the last decomposition.

The space $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ is a real Hilbert space under the square-sum chart norm fixed in [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]]. Apply [F5] to the bounded coercive form $b$ and the bounded functional $\psi\mapsto\langle f,\psi\rangle$; it yields a unique solution for every $f\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$.

routine_steps.claim: Let $u=D\phi$ and set $a=u^-_{\Omega^-}$. By [F3], $\|\gamma^-u^- -a\|_{H^{1/2}}\le C\|\nabla u^-\|_2$. By [F4], $\|\gamma^+u^+\|_{H^{1/2}}\le C\|\nabla u^+\|_2$. The jump condition gives $\phi+a=-(\gamma^-u^- -a)+\gamma^+u^+$, so $\inf_{c\in\mathbb R}\|\phi-c\|_{H^{1/2}}\le\|\phi+a\|_{H^{1/2}}\le C\mathcal E(D\phi)^{1/2}.$ Together with step 1.1 this proves the quotient ellipticity inequality. If $\phi$ is constant, the pair $(-\phi,0)$ belongs to $\mathcal A_\phi$ and has zero energy, so it is the unique minimizer and step 1.1 gives $W\phi=0$. Conversely, if $W\phi=0$, the ellipticity inequality makes $\phi$ a limit in $H^{1/2}$ of constants; the constant subspace is closed because it is finite dimensional, so $\phi$ is constant.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, $a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ a bounded coercive sesquilinear form (bilinear over $\mathbb R$), and $F$ a bounded functional with the test-linearity required by $a$. Let $V_h$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space with norm $\|\cdot\|_h$, not necessarily a subspace of $V$. Suppose the algebraic sum $X_h=V+V_h$ is equipped with a norm extending these norms, and $\widetilde a_h:X_h\times V_h\to\mathbb K$ is a bounded sesquilinear extension of a discrete form $a_h$ with bound $M_h$. Over $\mathbb C$, both forms are linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second; over $\mathbb R$, they are bilinear. Assume $a_h$ is coercive on $V_h$ with constant $\alpha_h>0$, and let $F_h$ be bounded on $V_h$ with the matching test-linearity. The exact and discrete equations have unique solutions $u$ and $u_h$, and

$$\|u-u_h\|_h\le(1+M_h/\alpha_h)\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_h+\delta_h^{\mathrm{nc}}(u)/\alpha_h,$$

where $\delta_h^{\mathrm{nc}}(u)=\sup_{w_h\in V_h\setminus\{0\}}|F_h(w_h)-\widetilde a_h(u,w_h)|/\|w_h\|_h$ when $V_h\ne\{0\}$, and $\delta_h^{\mathrm{nc}}(u):=0$ when $V_h=\{0\}$. The estimate requires the bounded extension and does not assert that every nonconforming, penalty, or discontinuous Galerkin form has one.

For a family of these problems, suppose $M_h\le\overline M<\infty$ and $\alpha_h\ge\underline\alpha>0$ uniformly. Writing $E_h=\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_h$, the uniform bound is
$$\|u-u_h\|_h\le(1+\overline M/\underline\alpha)E_h+\delta_h^{\mathrm{nc}}(u)/\underline\alpha.$$
Thus uniform control of $E_h$ and $\delta_h^{\mathrm{nc}}(u)$ gives a uniform error budget; if both tend to zero, the errors tend to zero, and if both are $O(h^p)$ for a fixed $p>0$, the error is $O(h^p)$. No rate is inferred without those approximation, residual, and stability bounds.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, let $a$ be a bounded coercive sesquilinear form on $H$ with constants $M,\alpha$ ([[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]]), and let $F:H\to\mathbb K$ be a bounded conjugate-linear functional with norm $\|F\|=\sup_{\|v\|\le1}|F(v)|$. Then there is a unique $u\in H$ with $$a(u,v)=F(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in H,$$ and it satisfies $\alpha\|u\|\le\|F\|$, that is $\|u\|\le\|F\|/\alpha$. The real bilinear case is the same statement with $a$ symmetric or not, $F$ a bounded linear functional, and the conjugation read as the identity.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For every $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$, with $\Gamma$ as in [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]], there is a unique $u=S\lambda\in\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ satisfying the weak single-layer equation of [[def-bem-laplace-layer-potentials-and-energy-spaces]]. It is harmonic on $\Omega^-$ and $\Omega^+$, its two traces agree, and its weak conormal traces satisfy
$$\partial_n^-u-\partial_n^+u=\lambda\quad\hbox{in }H^{-1/2}(\Gamma).$$
The trace operator $V\lambda:=\gamma u$ maps $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ boundedly into $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, and there are constants $C,c>0$ depending on $\Gamma$ such that
$$\|u\|_{\dot H^1}+\|V\lambda\|_{H^{1/2}}\le C\|\lambda\|_{H^{-1/2}},\qquad \langle\lambda,V\lambda\rangle_\Gamma\ge c\|\lambda\|_{H^{-1/2}}^2.$$
If $\lambda\in L^\infty(\Gamma)$ (in particular for facewise smooth densities reaching edges or discontinuous P0 densities), this weak potential agrees away from $\Gamma$ with $\int_\Gamma(4\pi|x-y|)^{-1}\lambda(y)dS_y$.

Let $\Gamma$ be a polyhedral boundary as in [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]]. A **conforming surface triangulation** $\mathcal T_h$ is a finite collection of nondegenerate closed planar triangles covering $\Gamma$, with disjoint relative interiors, such that two distinct triangles meet only in a common full edge, a common vertex, or not at all. For $T\in\mathcal T_h$, write $h_T=\operatorname{diam}(T)$ and let $\rho_T$ be the radius of the largest disk contained in $T$; the family is **shape regular** if $\sup_{h,T}h_T/\rho_T<\infty$, and **quasi-uniform** if $\inf_{h,T}h_T/h>0$ for $h=\max_{T\in\mathcal T_h}h_T$.

The conforming **P0 density space** is $X_h=\{\lambda_h\in L^2(\Gamma):\lambda_h|_T\text{ is constant for every }T\in\mathcal T_h\}$. The continuous inclusion $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)\hookrightarrow L^2(\Gamma)$ follows because each chart Bessel norm controls its L2 norm and the fixed partition is finite. Hence every $\lambda_h$ defines a bounded functional $v\mapsto\int_\Gamma\lambda_hv$ on $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$; thus $X_h\subset H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$. This inclusion makes the single-layer Galerkin method conforming in its energy space.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal T_h$ and $X_h$ be the surface mesh and P0 space from [[def-bem-surface-mesh-and-piecewise-constant-density-space]]. For an ordered target/source pair $(T,S)$ define its exact 3D Laplace single-layer matrix entry by
$$A_{TS}=\langle1_T,V1_S\rangle_\Gamma=\int_T\int_S\frac{1}{4\pi|x-y|}\,dS_y\,dS_x,$$
where the equality is proved for every panel pair by [[lem-bem-panel-pair-duffy-certificates]]. Supply a positive per-entry tolerance $\tau_{TS}$ and construct exactly one auditable certificate as follows.

Process the finite set of ordered panel pairs once in lexicographic mesh order. For each pair, first certify whether the panels coincide, share an edge, share a vertex, or are disjoint; if the incidence is unresolved, return **uncertified**. Use exact algebraic panel coordinates or provide the needed certified incidence, separation (for disjoint panels), denominator, and derivative bounds, together with outward arithmetic whose radii can be refined to zero. A missing required bound returns **uncertified**. After selecting a standard branch below, refine its quadrature and arithmetic certificates by levels $k=0,1,2,\ldots$ and accept the first level whose total error bound is at most $\tau_{TS}$. At each level refine precision until the combined node-value, evaluation and outward-arithmetic contribution to the entry bound is at most $2^{-k-1}\tau_{TS}$; charge the fiber-quadrature remainder separately.

- **Near certificate.** For coincident panels or panels sharing an edge or vertex, use the finite sign-cell/pulling-simplex identity of [[lem-bem-panel-pair-duffy-certificates]]. A disjoint pair may also use that lemma's smooth fallback whenever the whole-panel far-cluster condition below is unavailable. Each term is a reference-triangle integral $\int_R|z|^{-\alpha_m}q_m(z)dz$ with $\alpha_m<2$ and transformed amplitude $G_m\in C^{2n}([0,1]^2)$. Record the exact change-of-variables derivation, the supplied derivative bounds, and the positive Gaussian remainder $E_m$ from [[cor-duffy-weighted-product-gauss-error]]. If $\rho_m$ is the separately certified total of nested fiber, node-value and outward arithmetic radii, require $\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm near}=\sum_m|c_m|(E_m+\rho_m)\le\tau_{TS}$. A custom near identity may be accepted as a supplied finite certificate only after its identity, derivative bounds, every Gaussian hypothesis, and total error at most $\tau_{TS}$ have been verified; otherwise return **uncertified**. Do not run the standard refinement loop on a custom identity. For the standard panel-pair construction, every final exponent is $\alpha_m=0$.

- **Far certificate.** For disjoint panels, fix certified balls containing the entire source and target panels. Choose positive centroid rules on finite midpoint subdivisions and use [[lem-bem-far-panel-quadrature-residual]] to record the physical-kernel quadrature residual $\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm quad}$ and any separate outward evaluation radius $\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm eval}$. If the source nodes with physical charges $q_j=v_j/(4\pi)$ lie in $B(c,a)$ and the target nodes lie in $B(d,b)$ with the strict condition $R=|d-c|>a+b$, evaluate the single-cluster field of [[alg-three-dimensional-laplace-cluster-expansion]]. For $Q=\sum_j|q_j|$ and target weight sum $W_T$, record
$$\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm far}=\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm quad}+\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm eval}+W_T\frac{Q}{R-b}\frac{(a/(R-b))^{p+1}}{1-a/(R-b)}+\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm FMM-arith}.$$
The final term is the outward arithmetic radius of the finite cluster evaluation; it is zero only for an exact-arithmetic evaluation. At level $k$, use $m_T=m_S=p=k$ and refine outward precision as needed. If the whole-panel balls fail $R>a+b$, do not use this tail and instead use the disjoint smooth near fallback with $n=1$, subdividing both reference triangles at level $k$. No global multilevel or $O(N)$ work claim is made.

For a touching pair, use the standard identity and take $n=1$ in the weighted product rule on each similar-triangle subdivision at level $k$; when the opposite face has dimension three use $2^k$ midpoint subintervals for the finite fiber integral. Use midpoint subdivision, so each reference-triangle diameter is $2^{-k}$ times its original diameter, and use the per-level precision budget above. If a custom identity or any required hypothesis cannot be verified, return **uncertified**.

For every pair require its certified total error $\varepsilon_{TS}\le\tau_{TS}$. Given one successful certificate for every ordered pair, form $\widetilde A_h=(\widetilde A_{TS})$. If $\gamma_h>0$ is a certified lower norm bound satisfying
$$\|c\|_2\le\gamma_h^{-1}\left\|\sum_Tc_T1_T\right\|_{H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)},$$
compute the returned defect certificate
$$\delta_h=\gamma_h^{-2}\left(\sum_{T,S}\varepsilon_{TS}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
Any missing or unverified panel-pair geometry, identity, derivative bound, arithmetic radius or certificate returns **uncertified** and no matrix-defect claim. If no valid $\gamma_h$ is supplied, return the assembled matrix and its entrywise certificates without a matrix-defect bound. In particular, the batch-26 Duffy rule alone does not certify arbitrary coincident or edge-adjacent pairs.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice, and let $T,S$ be panels of the conforming surface triangulation in [[def-bem-surface-mesh-and-piecewise-constant-density-space]]. For $x\ne y$ put $G_3(x,y)=(4\pi|x-y|)^{-1}$ and define
$$\mathcal I_{TS}=\int_T\int_SG_3(x,y)\,dS_y\,dS_x.$$
The integral is absolutely convergent. If $V$ is the single-layer operator of [[def-bem-calderon-boundary-operators]], then
$$\mathcal I_{TS}=\langle1_T,V1_S\rangle_\Gamma.$$

For coincident panels, panels sharing a full edge, and panels sharing a vertex, the exact affine parameter integral for $\mathcal I_{TS}$ has a finite decomposition into integrals
$$c_m\int_R q_m(z)\,dz,\qquad R=\{(x,y):0\le y\le x\le1\},$$
where $c_m>0$, each $q_m$ is smooth on a neighborhood of $R$, and every integral is the Duffy-transformed case with exponent $\alpha=0<2$. The decomposition includes every singular-face dimension: in each four-simplex of the finite decomposition the zero face may have dimension $0$, $1$, or $2$. If $T$ and $S$ are disjoint, their positive separation instead gives one smooth reference-triangle integral with the same exponent $\alpha=0$.

The constructions supply explicit lower bounds for every denominator and explicit derivative bounds for every required amplitude. Given exact algebraic panel coordinates and any positive absolute tolerance $\varepsilon$, the finite nested Gaussian procedure described in the proof terminates with an outward-certified value $\widetilde{\mathcal I}_{TS}$ satisfying $|\mathcal I_{TS}-\widetilde{\mathcal I}_{TS}|\le\varepsilon$. For other coordinate representations, the procedure has the same guarantee when certified finite incidence, nondegeneracy, separation, and arithmetic bounds are supplied as input. It makes no termination claim for deciding incidences from an uncertified arbitrary-real oracle.

For $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ define the Laplace Calderon boundary operators by
$$V\lambda=\gamma S\lambda,\qquad K\phi=\tfrac12(\gamma^-D\phi+\gamma^+D\phi),$$
$$K'\lambda=\tfrac12(\partial_n^-S\lambda+\partial_n^+S\lambda),\qquad W\phi=-\partial_n^-D\phi=-\partial_n^+D\phi.$$
Here $\gamma S\lambda$ is the common trace, conormal traces use the orientation of [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]], and the last equality is meaningful because the weak double layer has a common conormal derivative. This page uses the real duality pairing between $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$. The well-definedness and bounded mapping properties of $V,K,K',W$ are proved in [[thm-bem-calderon-mapping-and-jump-identities]].

Let $T,S$ be disjoint nondegenerate compact triangles in a conforming surface mesh, let $d$ be supplied with $0<d\le\operatorname{dist}(T,S)$, and set
$$A_{TS}=\frac1{4\pi}\int_T\int_S\frac{1}{|x-y|}\,dS_y\,dS_x.$$
Apply $m_T$ and $m_S$ successive midpoint refinements to $T$ and $S$, respectively. The resulting subtriangles have maximum diameters $h_T=2^{-m_T}\operatorname{diam}(T)$ and $h_S=2^{-m_S}\operatorname{diam}(S)$. Give each subtriangle its area as a positive weight and its centroid as its node, obtaining rules $(x_i,w_i)$ and $(y_j,v_j)$. Then
$$B_{TS}=\sum_i\sum_j\frac{w_iv_j}{4\pi|x_i-y_j|}$$
satisfies
$$|A_{TS}-B_{TS}|\le\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm quad}:=\frac{|T||S|(h_T+h_S)}{4\pi d^2}.$$
Repeated midpoint subdivision makes this residual tend to zero. For exact algebraic panel coordinates, a supplied strict algebraic lower bound for $d$ and outward interval evaluation therefore gives an effective certificate at every positive tolerance; for other coordinates the corresponding certified separation and arithmetic bounds are required.

For the physical kernel, if the source nodes have charges $q_j=v_j/(4\pi)$ in $B(c,a)$ and the target nodes lie in $B(d_c,b)$ with $R=|d_c-c|>a+b$, then the literal single-cluster evaluator of [[alg-three-dimensional-laplace-cluster-expansion]] has $Q=\sum_j|q_j|$ and target-weight sum $W_T=\sum_iw_i$. Its contribution to the entry error is at most
$$W_T\frac{Q}{R-b}\frac{(a/(R-b))^{p+1}}{1-a/(R-b)}.$$
Add separately certified quadrature, node-evaluation and outward-arithmetic radii. This is a single-cluster estimate, not a multilevel or global complexity result.

Assume Countable Choice, let $\alpha<2$, $\rho=1-\alpha$, $n\ge1$, and let $G\in C^{2n}$ in each coordinate on $[0,1]^2$. Let $\widetilde p_{n,\rho}$ and $\widetilde p_{n,0}$ be the monic node polynomials of the pushed-forward Gauss–Jacobi rules for $r^\rho dr$ and $ds$, respectively. Define
$$M_\rho=\int_0^1r^\rho dr=\frac1{\rho+1},\quad K_\rho=\frac1{(2n)!_{\mathbb R}}\int_0^1\widetilde p_{n,\rho}(r)^2r^\rho dr,\quad K_0=\frac1{(2n)!_{\mathbb R}}\int_0^1\widetilde p_{n,0}(s)^2ds.$$
Then the rule of [[alg-duffy-weighted-product-gauss-quadrature]] satisfies
$$\left|\int_T\|(x,y)\|_2^{-\alpha}q(x,y)\,dx\,dy-Q_{n,\alpha}^{D}(G)\right| \le K_\rho\|\partial_r^{2n}G\|_\infty+M_\rho K_0\|\partial_s^{2n}G\|_\infty,$$
where $G$ is the transformed amplitude from [[thm-duffy-weak-singularity-transform]].

For the single-cluster evaluator of [[alg-three-dimensional-laplace-cluster-expansion]], let $Q=\sum_{j\in J}|q_j|$. If a target satisfies $r=|x-c|>a$, then its potential error obeys
$$|U(x)-\widetilde U_p(x)|\le\frac{Q}{r}\frac{(a/r)^{p+1}}{1-a/r}.$$
If a target region is contained in a ball of radius $b$ centered at $d$, with $R=|d-c|>a+b$, then every target in the region has error at most
$$\frac{Q}{R-b}\frac{\bigl(a/(R-b)\bigr)^{p+1}}{1-a/(R-b)}.$$
Let $S=|J|$ and let $T_0$ be the number of targets. Under the monomial-coefficient evaluation convention of the algorithm, forming moments and evaluating the truncated field costs $O((S+T_0)(p+1)^4)$ arithmetic operations after the basis coefficient arrays have been prepared. If all basis values at sources and targets are supplied, the coefficient accumulation and expansion evaluation alone cost $O((S+T_0)(p+1)^2)$. This is a single-cluster estimate; it is not a 3D multilevel FMM tree complexity theorem.

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

Assume [[def-countable-choice|Countable Choice]].

Let $\Omega^-$ be a nonempty bounded connected open subset of $\mathbb R^3$ whose boundary $\Gamma=\partial\Omega^-$ is a compact connected orientable Lipschitz surface. A **Lipschitz graph chart** is a rigid coordinate change in which $\Gamma$ is the graph $x_3=\psi(x_1,x_2)$ of a Lipschitz function on an open subset of $\mathbb R^2$, with $\Omega^-$ on one side of that graph. A **polyhedral boundary** is such a boundary made from finitely many planar polygonal faces meeting along edges and vertices; all surface-discretization claims below use this polyhedral subclass. Put $\Omega^+=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline{\Omega^-}$ and assume $\Omega^+$ is connected. For the fixed-atlas space conventions below, the boundary data include a compatible Borel surface measure $dS$ and an almost-everywhere unit outward normal $n$, with the following graph realizations and bounded positive graph area densities on every chosen chart. These compatible realizations are supplied data for the Countable-Choice space assertions, not conclusions from bare Lipschitzness under Countable Choice. Under the Axiom of Choice, [[lem-bem-lipschitz-graph-sobolev-and-green-interface]] constructs them for every compact Lipschitz boundary and proves their compatibility; the general analytical trace and layer theorems state that axiom. On polyhedral charts the data are directly the finite face areas and face normals. The normal points from $\Omega^-$ into $\Omega^+$. In a rigid chart with $\Omega^-$ above the graph $x_3=\psi(x_1,x_2)$ it is $n=(\partial_1\psi,\partial_2\psi,-1)/\sqrt{1+|\nabla\psi|^2}$ almost everywhere; reverse the sign when the domain is below the graph. Rigid coordinates transform this vector to physical coordinates. The graph surface measure is $dS=\sqrt{1+|\nabla\psi|^2}\,dx_1dx_2$. Compatibility on overlaps is part of the fixed boundary data; the cited AC graph theorem proves it for arbitrary Lipschitz charts. On a polyhedron these are the face-area measure and outward face normals.

Fix a finite Lipschitz graph atlas $\{(U_j,\psi_j)\}_{j=1}^J$, with surface parametrizations $\Phi_j(z)=(z,\psi_j(z))$ in the rigid chart coordinates, and a subordinate finite Lipschitz partition of unity $\{\chi_j\}_{j=1}^J$ whose chartwise supports have positive distance from the chart edges. On $\mathbb R^2$, use the real subspace of the real-order Bessel-potential completion in [[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]]. Its published norm uses the weight $(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$. Fix here the equivalent Hilbert norm
$$q(g)^2=\int_{\mathbb R^2}(1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{1/2}|\widehat g(\xi)|^2d\xi.$$
The inequalities $(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}\le(1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{1/2}\le2\pi(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$ identify the same completion and classes under the negative-sign $2\pi$ Fourier convention of [[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-fractional-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]. Define the real space $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ by requiring every localized chart pullback $g_j=(\chi_jg)\circ\Phi_j$, extended by zero outside its chart, to belong to that Euclidean space, and fix the **square-sum chart norm**
$$\|g\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}^2=\sum_{j=1}^J q(g_j)^2.$$
Its inner product is the sum of the real weighted Fourier inner products. The following fixed-data norm and completeness assertions use only Countable Choice and the supplied compatible measure with bounded positive chart densities; they make no geometry-existence or atlas-compatibility assertion under that weaker axiom. This Hilbert norm is equivalent to the finite sum of chart norms: $(\sum_jq(g_j)^2)^{1/2}\le\sum_jq(g_j)\le\sqrt J(\sum_jq(g_j)^2)^{1/2}$. It controls $L^2(\Gamma)$, because graph surface Jacobians are bounded above and below and $g=\sum_j\chi_jg$. It is complete: a chart-norm Cauchy sequence has a global $L^2$ limit by that bound; its localized pullbacks converge in $L^2$ to the pullbacks of this limit, while completeness of each Euclidean weighted space gives convergence in each $q$ norm. The two limits agree, so the limit belongs to the defined chart space and convergence holds in the finite square sum.

Let real $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ be the continuous real dual, with its operator norm and pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_\Gamma$; the dual of this real Hilbert space is Hilbert by [[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]. The interior and exterior traces of an $H^1$ function are denoted $\gamma^-u$ and $\gamma^+u$; their common chartwise trace space is $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ once the applicable trace theorem is proved. This fixed-atlas chart-space convention applies to the stated Lipschitz geometry, including its polyhedral and $C^2$ subclasses. It defines the Hilbert and dual norms; no boundary trace or lifting theorem is assumed by that convention.

The complex space is the Hilbert complexification of the real space: $\|g_1+ig_2\|^2=\|g_1\|^2+\|g_2\|^2$. Its $H^{-1/2}$ is the continuous conjugate dual, with pairing linear in the density and conjugate-linear in the trace, extending the real pairing. A complex density is a distribution via the **bilinear** test action $T_\lambda(v)=\langle\lambda,\overline v\rangle_\Gamma$. For either scalar field the continuous realization $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)\subset L^2(\Gamma)\subset H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ uses $\langle f,g\rangle_\Gamma=\int_\Gamma f\overline g\,dS$ in the complex case and $\int_\Gamma fg\,dS$ in the real case. These inclusions follow from the just-proved $H^{1/2}\to L^2$ bound and Cauchy–Schwarz.

No smoothness at edges or vertices is included in this definition. The normal is only used almost everywhere. On every Lipschitz boundary use the intrinsic graph surface measure just specified, with the chart partition; on a polyhedral boundary it equals the sum of planar face-area measures. The general Lipschitz class and its $C^2$ subclass therefore use the same measure and orientation conventions.

derivations.claim: For a standard near certificate, [F5] supplies the exact identity; a custom certificate supplies it as an audited hypothesis. In either case each exponent and transformed amplitude meet [F7], so the positive Duffy rule error is bounded by $E_m$. Add the separately certified nested fiber, node-evaluation and outward arithmetic radii with the triangle inequality; the certificate condition gives $|A_{TS}-\widetilde A_{TS}|\le\sum_m|c_m|(E_m+\rho_m)=\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm near}\le\tau_{TS}$.

For a far certificate, [F6] bounds the difference between the exact entry and the positive centroid sum by $\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm quad}+\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm eval}$. Under the strict ball condition, [F8] bounds the point-cluster error uniformly over the target ball. Multiplying by the positive target weights and adding the outward arithmetic radius gives the remaining terms in $\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm far}$. The total is at most $\tau_{TS}$ by the certificate condition; if $R\le a+b$, no FMM tail is used.

Apply [F1] with exact form $a$, exact load $F$, and conforming subspace $X_h$. It gives the unique exact solution $u$, the unique exact Galerkin solution $u_h$, and $\|u-u_h\|_H\le(1+C/c)\inf_{v_h\in X_h}\|u-v_h\|_H$, since the consistency defect is zero.

The perturbation bound and coercivity of $a$ imply $\widetilde a_h(v_h,v_h)\ge(c-\delta)\|v_h\|_H^2$ for all $v_h$. Also $|\widetilde a_h(v_h,w_h)|\le(C+\delta)\|v_h\|_H\|w_h\|_H$, and $\|\widetilde F_h\|\le\|F_h\|+\eta$. Lax–Milgram [F2] therefore gives a unique perturbed solution $\widetilde u_h$.

For a standard touching pair, [F5] gives finitely many smooth amplitudes with fixed derivative bounds. At level $k$, midpoint triangle subdivision and the $n=1$ pure-derivative remainder give total triangle error at most $C_{TS}4^{-k}$; where an opposite face has dimension three, its $2^k$ fiber midpoints add at most $C_{TS}4^{-k}$. The disjoint smooth fallback has the same bound after subdividing both reference triangles. For the far branch, [F6] gives centroid error at most $C_{TS}2^{-k}$. The fixed whole-panel balls give $q=a/(R-b)<1$, and positivity fixes $Q=|S|/(4\pi)$ and $W_T=|T|$ independently of level; hence [F8] gives a tail at most $C_{TS}q^{k+1}$ (zero if $a=0$). By [F4] the combined evaluation and arithmetic radius is at most $2^{-k-1}\tau_{TS}$, reached in finite precision refinement by hypothesis. Each total therefore tends to zero, so the first accepted level is finite for every $\tau_{TS}>0$. The ordered panel-pair set is finite, and a custom identity uses a supplied finite certificate rather than this loop. This proves the stated termination assertion.

Write $E_{TS}=A_{TS}-\widetilde A_{TS}$. For coefficient vectors $c,d$, finite Cauchy–Schwarz gives $|d^TEc|\le\left(\sum_{T,S}|E_{TS}|^2\right)^{1/2}\|c\|_2\|d\|_2$. The certified entry bounds imply $|E_{TS}|\le\varepsilon_{TS}$. The supplied lower norm bound in [F4] gives $\|c\|_2\le\gamma_h^{-1}\|\sum_Sc_S1_S\|_{H^{-1/2}}$ and the corresponding bound for $d$. Substitute both inequalities and take the supremum over unit $H^{-1/2}$ densities to obtain the bilinear operator-defect bound $\delta_h$. If a pair has no successful certificate, steps 1.1–1.2 provide no bound for that entry, so the procedure correctly returns uncertified.

Test the perturbed equation with $\widetilde u_h$. Then $(c-\delta)\|\widetilde u_h\|_H^2\le(\|F_h\|_{X_h'}+\eta)\|\widetilde u_h\|_H$, so $\|\widetilde u_h\|_H\le(\|F_h\|_{X_h'}+\eta)/(c-\delta)$; this also holds if $\widetilde u_h=0$.

Put $e_h=u_h-\widetilde u_h$. Subtracting the perturbed equation from the exact discrete equation gives $a(e_h,w_h)=F_h(w_h)-\widetilde F_h(w_h)+(\widetilde a_h-a)(\widetilde u_h,w_h)$. Take $w_h=e_h$. If $e_h\ne0$, coercivity and the two defects give $\|e_h\|_H\le c^{-1}(\eta+\delta\|\widetilde u_h\|_H)$; if $e_h=0$ the same inequality holds. Substitute step 2.2 to obtain $\|e_h\|_H\le c^{-1}(\eta+\delta(\|F_h\|_{X_h'}+\eta)/(c-\delta))$.

By the triangle inequality, $\|u-\widetilde u_h\|_H\le\|u-u_h\|_H+\|e_h\|_H$. Apply step 1.3 and step 3.1 to get the displayed bound. In the BEM specialization, [F3] verifies the exact-form hypotheses and the entrywise and form estimates in steps 1.1–2.1 verify that the successful assembly defect is the $\delta$ required here.

citations.quote: For $x\ne y$ in $\mathbb R^3$, the Newton kernel is $G_3(x,y)=(4\pi|x-y|)^{-1}$. Its distributional fundamental-solution property $-\Delta_xG_3(x,y)=\delta_y$ is proved in [[lem-bem-newtonian-kernel-is-fundamental-solution]]. The kernel fixes the sign and $4\pi$ normalization for every three-dimensional layer operator on this page.

Let $(D,\varphi)$ be a regular surface patch and let $q$ be a continuous real-valued function on $\varphi[D]$. For a continuous scalar field $q$ on the patch image, $\int_Sq\,dS:=\int_D(q\circ\varphi)J_\varphi$, and $\operatorname{Area}(S):=\int_DJ_\varphi$.

Here $S$ denotes the patch with its chosen parametrization. Both integrands are bounded and Riemann integrable on the compact Jordan region $D$ by continuity ([[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]). Boundary values are included in the parameter integral but may be changed on the content-zero boundary without changing its value.

The functions $\sin$ and $\cos$ are differentiable on $\mathbb R$, with
$$(\sin x)'=\cos x,\qquad(\cos x)'=-\sin x.$$
Also $\sin0=0$ and $\cos0=1$.

Let $a < b$ be reals, let $G : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at every
point of $[a,b]$ as a function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-derivative]]; at $a$ and $b$
this is the one-sided derivative), let $f := G'$, and suppose $f$ is integrable
on $[a,b]$ ([[def-darboux-integral]]). Then

$$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**Both hypotheses are needed and neither is removable.** A function may be
differentiable everywhere with $G'$ not integrable — then the left-hand side does
not exist (an everywhere differentiable function with unbounded derivative) — and an
integrable $f$ need not be the derivative of anything
(the sign function); both witnesses are on the
companion page.

**No continuity of $f$ is assumed**, which is what makes this the working form:
the theorem evaluates $\int_a^b f$ for every integrable derivative, not only for
continuous integrands.

derivations.claim: For $r=|x|>0$, spherical coordinates centered on the axis through $x$ give $S1(x)=\frac{R^2}{2}\int_{-1}^1(r^2+R^2-2rRt)^{-1/2}dt=\frac{R}{2r}(r+R-|r-R|).$ If $r<R$ this equals $R$, and if $r>R$ it equals $R^2/r$; at $r=R$ the same convergent improper integral gives $R$, and at $r=0$ the constant kernel $1/(4\pi R)$ times the parametrized area $4\pi R^2$ gives $R$.

routine_steps.claim: Differentiating the two radial formulas gives $\partial_rS1=0$ for $r<R$ and $\partial_rS1=-R^2/r^2$ for $r>R$. Their boundary limits are $0$ and $-1$, so $\partial_n^-S1-\partial_n^+S1=1=\lambda$. This direct smooth-sphere calculation checks the kernel normalization and jump orientation independently of the polyhedral theorem.

citations.quote: For $x\ne y$ in $\mathbb R^3$, the Newton kernel is $G_3(x,y)=(4\pi|x-y|)^{-1}$. Its distributional fundamental-solution property $-\Delta_xG_3(x,y)=\delta_y$ is proved in [[lem-bem-newtonian-kernel-is-fundamental-solution]]. The kernel fixes the sign and $4\pi$ normalization for every three-dimensional layer operator on this page.

For $R>0$, let $S_R=\{y\in\mathbb R^3:|y|=R\}$ and take density $\lambda=1$. The classical Newton single-layer potential is
$$S1(x)=\int_{S_R}\frac{1}{4\pi|x-y|}\,dS_y=\begin{cases}R,&|x|\le R,\\ R^2/|x|,&|x|\ge R.\end{cases}$$
It is continuous on $S_R$ with trace $R$. With outward radial normal, the interior and exterior normal derivatives at the sphere are $0$ and $-1$, respectively, so their difference is $1$, the density.

Let $a<b$ and $c<d$. Suppose $g,h:[a,b]\times[c,d]\to\mathbb R$ are continuous and, for every fixed $t\in[c,d]$, the function $x\mapsto g(x,t)$ is differentiable on $(a,b)$ with derivative $h(x,t)$. Define

$$G(x):=\int_c^d g(x,t)\,dt.$$

Then $G$ is differentiable on $[a,b]$ as a function on that interval and

$$G'(x)=\int_c^d h(x,t)\,dt\qquad(x\in[a,b]).$$

At $a$ and $b$ the derivative is relative and one-sided. The derivative hypothesis is imposed only for interior parameter values; continuity of $h$ supplies its endpoint values.

Let $(D,\varphi)$ be a regular surface patch and let $q$ be a continuous real-valued function on $\varphi[D]$. For a continuous scalar field $q$ on the patch image, $\int_Sq\,dS:=\int_D(q\circ\varphi)J_\varphi$, and $\operatorname{Area}(S):=\int_DJ_\varphi$.

Here $S$ denotes the patch with its chosen parametrization. Both integrands are bounded and Riemann integrable on the compact Jordan region $D$ by continuity ([[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]). Boundary values are included in the parameter integral but may be changed on the content-zero boundary without changing its value.

derivations.claim: The single-layer trace and conormal sign are exactly [F2]. For the double layer put $U_R(x)=\int_{S_R}G_3(x,y)dS_y$ and $D_R1(x)=\int_{S_R}\partial_{n_y}G_3(x,y)dS_y$. In sphere parameters $y=R\omega$, differentiating $R^2G_3(x,R\omega)$ by [F3] gives $\partial_RU_R=D_R1+(2/R)U_R$: the kernel derivative is the outward source-normal derivative, and the second term differentiates area density.

For fixed $|x|<1$ and $R$ sufficiently near one, [F2] gives $U_R(x)=R$, so $D_R1=1-2=-1$. For fixed $|x|>1$ it gives $U_R(x)=R^2/|x|$, so $D_R1=2R/|x|-(2/R)(R^2/|x|)=0$. At $R=1$ the two potentials are constant on their respective sides; therefore their trace jump is $-1$ and both normal derivatives are zero. This proves both signs without adding a divergence-theorem axiom to the classical example.

Assume [[def-countable-choice|Countable Choice]].

Let $\Omega^-$ be a nonempty bounded connected open subset of $\mathbb R^3$ whose boundary $\Gamma=\partial\Omega^-$ is a compact connected orientable Lipschitz surface. A **Lipschitz graph chart** is a rigid coordinate change in which $\Gamma$ is the graph $x_3=\psi(x_1,x_2)$ of a Lipschitz function on an open subset of $\mathbb R^2$, with $\Omega^-$ on one side of that graph. A **polyhedral boundary** is such a boundary made from finitely many planar polygonal faces meeting along edges and vertices; all surface-discretization claims below use this polyhedral subclass. Put $\Omega^+=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline{\Omega^-}$ and assume $\Omega^+$ is connected. For the fixed-atlas space conventions below, the boundary data include a compatible Borel surface measure $dS$ and an almost-everywhere unit outward normal $n$, with the following graph realizations and bounded positive graph area densities on every chosen chart. These compatible realizations are supplied data for the Countable-Choice space assertions, not conclusions from bare Lipschitzness under Countable Choice. Under the Axiom of Choice, [[lem-bem-lipschitz-graph-sobolev-and-green-interface]] constructs them for every compact Lipschitz boundary and proves their compatibility; the general analytical trace and layer theorems state that axiom. On polyhedral charts the data are directly the finite face areas and face normals. The normal points from $\Omega^-$ into $\Omega^+$. In a rigid chart with $\Omega^-$ above the graph $x_3=\psi(x_1,x_2)$ it is $n=(\partial_1\psi,\partial_2\psi,-1)/\sqrt{1+|\nabla\psi|^2}$ almost everywhere; reverse the sign when the domain is below the graph. Rigid coordinates transform this vector to physical coordinates. The graph surface measure is $dS=\sqrt{1+|\nabla\psi|^2}\,dx_1dx_2$. Compatibility on overlaps is part of the fixed boundary data; the cited AC graph theorem proves it for arbitrary Lipschitz charts. On a polyhedron these are the face-area measure and outward face normals.

Fix a finite Lipschitz graph atlas $\{(U_j,\psi_j)\}_{j=1}^J$, with surface parametrizations $\Phi_j(z)=(z,\psi_j(z))$ in the rigid chart coordinates, and a subordinate finite Lipschitz partition of unity $\{\chi_j\}_{j=1}^J$ whose chartwise supports have positive distance from the chart edges. On $\mathbb R^2$, use the real subspace of the real-order Bessel-potential completion in [[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]]. Its published norm uses the weight $(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$. Fix here the equivalent Hilbert norm
$$q(g)^2=\int_{\mathbb R^2}(1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{1/2}|\widehat g(\xi)|^2d\xi.$$
The inequalities $(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}\le(1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{1/2}\le2\pi(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$ identify the same completion and classes under the negative-sign $2\pi$ Fourier convention of [[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-fractional-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]. Define the real space $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ by requiring every localized chart pullback $g_j=(\chi_jg)\circ\Phi_j$, extended by zero outside its chart, to belong to that Euclidean space, and fix the **square-sum chart norm**
$$\|g\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}^2=\sum_{j=1}^J q(g_j)^2.$$
Its inner product is the sum of the real weighted Fourier inner products. The following fixed-data norm and completeness assertions use only Countable Choice and the supplied compatible measure with bounded positive chart densities; they make no geometry-existence or atlas-compatibility assertion under that weaker axiom. This Hilbert norm is equivalent to the finite sum of chart norms: $(\sum_jq(g_j)^2)^{1/2}\le\sum_jq(g_j)\le\sqrt J(\sum_jq(g_j)^2)^{1/2}$. It controls $L^2(\Gamma)$, because graph surface Jacobians are bounded above and below and $g=\sum_j\chi_jg$. It is complete: a chart-norm Cauchy sequence has a global $L^2$ limit by that bound; its localized pullbacks converge in $L^2$ to the pullbacks of this limit, while completeness of each Euclidean weighted space gives convergence in each $q$ norm. The two limits agree, so the limit belongs to the defined chart space and convergence holds in the finite square sum.

Let real $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ be the continuous real dual, with its operator norm and pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_\Gamma$; the dual of this real Hilbert space is Hilbert by [[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]. The interior and exterior traces of an $H^1$ function are denoted $\gamma^-u$ and $\gamma^+u$; their common chartwise trace space is $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ once the applicable trace theorem is proved. This fixed-atlas chart-space convention applies to the stated Lipschitz geometry, including its polyhedral and $C^2$ subclasses. It defines the Hilbert and dual norms; no boundary trace or lifting theorem is assumed by that convention.

The complex space is the Hilbert complexification of the real space: $\|g_1+ig_2\|^2=\|g_1\|^2+\|g_2\|^2$. Its $H^{-1/2}$ is the continuous conjugate dual, with pairing linear in the density and conjugate-linear in the trace, extending the real pairing. A complex density is a distribution via the **bilinear** test action $T_\lambda(v)=\langle\lambda,\overline v\rangle_\Gamma$. For either scalar field the continuous realization $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)\subset L^2(\Gamma)\subset H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ uses $\langle f,g\rangle_\Gamma=\int_\Gamma f\overline g\,dS$ in the complex case and $\int_\Gamma fg\,dS$ in the real case. These inclusions follow from the just-proved $H^{1/2}\to L^2$ bound and Cauchy–Schwarz.

No smoothness at edges or vertices is included in this definition. The normal is only used almost everywhere. On every Lipschitz boundary use the intrinsic graph surface measure just specified, with the chart partition; on a polyhedral boundary it equals the sum of planar face-area measures. The general Lipschitz class and its $C^2$ subclass therefore use the same measure and orientation conventions.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n \ge 1$,
let $S^{n-1} \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be the unit sphere, and let $\sigma$ be the
set function of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]. Then $\sigma$
is a finite Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$, and for every Borel measurable
$f : \mathbb R^n \to [0,\infty]$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^n} f(x)\,d\lambda_n(x) = \int_0^\infty \int_{S^{n-1}} f(r\omega) r^{n-1}\,d\sigma(\omega)\,dr.$$
Moreover, $\sigma$ is the unique Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$ with this
property.

routine_steps.claim: In polar coordinates the cross-sectional Laplacian is $\partial_{rr}+r^{-1}\partial_r+r^{-2}\partial_{\theta\theta}$. For $u=r^\alpha\sin(\alpha\theta)$, the three terms sum to $[\alpha(\alpha-1)+\alpha-\alpha^2]r^{\alpha-2}\sin(\alpha\theta)=0$; the $z$ derivative is zero. Also $u(r,0,z)=u(r,\omega,z)=0$ because $\alpha\omega=\pi$. Thus it is harmonic with zero side trace in the local geometry [F1].

The squared transverse gradient is $|\nabla_{r,\theta}u|^2=\alpha^2r^{2\alpha-2}$, so its local integral is a constant times $\int_0^{r_0}r^{2\alpha-1}dr<\infty$ for $\alpha>0$; $u$ itself is also square integrable. On the other hand, $u_{rr}=\alpha(\alpha-1)r^{\alpha-2}\sin(\alpha\theta)$ is nonzero on a set of angles of positive measure, and its squared integral contains $c\int_0^{r_0}r^{2\alpha-3}dr=\infty$ because $\alpha<1$. Hence $u\in H^1$ locally but $u\notin H^2$ near the edge.

$$\|F_h\|_{X_h'}=\sup_{\substack{w_h\in X_h\\\|w_h\|_H\le1}}|F_h(w_h)|.$$
Let $u\in H$ solve $a(u,w)=F(w)$ for all $w\in H$, and let $u_h\in X_h$ be its exact Galerkin solution. Suppose a bilinear form $\widetilde a_h:X_h\times X_h\to\mathbb R$ and load $\widetilde F_h\in X_h'$ satisfy
$$|\widetilde a_h(v_h,w_h)-a(v_h,w_h)|\le\delta\|v_h\|_H\|w_h\|_H,\qquad |\widetilde F_h(w_h)-F_h(w_h)|\le\eta\|w_h\|_H$$
for all $v_h,w_h\in X_h$, with $0\le\delta<c$. The perturbed equation $\widetilde a_h(\widetilde u_h,w_h)=\widetilde F_h(w_h)$ has a unique solution and
$$\|u-\widetilde u_h\|_H\le(1+C/c)\inf_{v_h\in X_h}\|u-v_h\|_H+\frac1c\left(\eta+\frac{\delta(\|F_h\|_{X_h'}+\eta)}{c-\delta}\right).$$
Independently of the condition $\delta<c$ in the variational estimate, for a successful assembly in [[alg-bem-certified-inexact-matrix-assembly]], every near or far certificate gives $|A_{TS}-\widetilde A_{TS}|\le\varepsilon_{TS}\le\tau_{TS}$. If the supplied $\gamma_h>0$ satisfies $\|c\|_2\le\gamma_h^{-1}\|\sum_Tc_T1_T\|_{H^{-1/2}}$, then the returned value
$$\delta_h=\gamma_h^{-2}\left(\sum_{T,S}\varepsilon_{TS}^2\right)^{1/2}$$
bounds the bilinear form defect in the fixed $H^{-1/2}$ norm. This guarantee includes the exact near-pair identities and all derivative, nested-fiber, evaluation and arithmetic errors, and uses the far tail only under $R>a+b$; an uncertified output supplies no such bound.

Let $\mathbb S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ with its usual surface-area measure $dS$, normalized so $\int_{\mathbb S^2}dS=4\pi$. For an integer $\ell\ge0$, let $\mathcal H_\ell$ be the complex vector space of restrictions to $\mathbb S^2$ of homogeneous degree-$\ell$ polynomials $P(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ satisfying $\Delta P=0$. Give $\mathcal H_\ell$ the inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb S^2}f\overline g\,dS$, linear in the first argument. An orthonormal basis is not fixed by this definition; the addition-theorem item proves that $\dim\mathcal H_\ell=2\ell+1$ and that such a finite basis exists.

If $Y_{\ell m}\in\mathcal H_\ell$ is later chosen from an orthonormal basis and $v\ne0$, its associated homogeneous harmonic polynomial is $H_{\ell m}(v)=|v|^\ell Y_{\ell m}(v/|v|)$. At $v=0$ use the polynomial value: $H_{00}(0)=Y_{00}$ and $H_{\ell m}(0)=0$ for $\ell>0$. This is the regular-solid-harmonic convention used in the 3D evaluator.

For every integer $\ell\ge0$, the space $\mathcal H_\ell$ of [[def-three-dimensional-spherical-harmonic-space]] has dimension $2\ell+1$. For any orthonormal basis $\{Y_{\ell m}:-\ell\le m\le\ell\}$, there is a basis-independent normalized zonal polynomial $P_\ell$ such that
$$\sum_{m=-\ell}^{\ell}Y_{\ell m}(\omega)\overline{Y_{\ell m}(\omega')}=\frac{2\ell+1}{4\pi}P_\ell(\omega\cdot\omega'),\qquad P_\ell(1)=1.$$
It obeys $|P_\ell(t)|\le1$ for $-1\le t\le1$ and the generating identity
$$\frac1{\sqrt{1-2rt+r^2}}=\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}r^\ell P_\ell(t),\qquad -1\le t\le1,\quad 0\le r<1.$$
Let $K$ be a nonempty compact metric space and let $A\subseteq C(K,\mathbb R)$ be a unital subalgebra which separates points. Then $A$ is dense in $C(K,\mathbb R)$ for the supremum metric.
For $n\ge1$, $c\in\mathbb{R}^n$, and $r>0$, the Euclidean closed ball $\overline B_2(c,r)$ and Euclidean sphere $S_2(c,r)$ are compact.

derivations.claim: For a homogeneous polynomial $Q_n$ of degree $n$, direct differentiation and Euler's identity give $\Delta(|x|^{2j}Q_n)=2j(2n+2j+1)|x|^{2j-2}Q_n+|x|^{2j}\Delta Q_n$. For homogeneous $P$ of degree $n$, set $H=P+\sum_{j=1}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}a_j|x|^{2j}\Delta^jP$, where $a_0=1$ and $a_{j+1}=-a_j/[2(j+1)(2n-2j-1)]$. Substitution into the displayed identity makes the coefficient of each $|x|^{2j}\Delta^{j+1}P$ equal to $a_j+2(j+1)(2n-2j-1)a_{j+1}=0$; the last Laplacian power vanishes by degree. Thus $H$ is homogeneous harmonic and $P-H$ is divisible by $|x|^2$. Induction on degree shows that restrictions of polynomials are finite sums of elements of the spaces $\mathcal H_j$.

The polar-coordinate identity $\Delta=\partial_{rr}+2r^{-1}\partial_r+r^{-2}\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}$ applied to $r^\ell Y(\omega)$, whose extension is harmonic by [F1], gives $\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}Y=-\ell(\ell+1)Y$. On the sphere, integration by parts gives $\langle v,\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}w\rangle=\langle\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}v,w\rangle$: in $(\theta,\phi)$ coordinates integrate the $\phi$ derivative over its period and the $\theta$ term with weight $\sin\theta$; the pole boundary terms vanish because smooth functions and their spherical gradients are bounded while $\sin\theta\to0$. Distinct degrees have distinct eigenvalues, so their spaces are orthogonal.

Choose a finite orthonormal basis from [F2] and write $g=\sum_m c_mY_{\ell m}$. Cauchy–Schwarz gives $|g(\omega)|^2\le(\sum_m|c_m|^2)(\sum_m|Y_{\ell m}(\omega)|^2)$. Orthonormality identifies the first sum with $\|g\|_2^2$, and [F2] gives the second as $(2\ell+1)/(4\pi)$. Taking the supremum proves the evaluation bound.

Real polynomial restrictions contain constants and separate distinct points of $\mathbb S^2$ by a coordinate function. Compactness and [F3] make them dense in real $C(\mathbb S^2)$; applying this separately to real and imaginary parts gives density in complex $C(\mathbb S^2)$. By step 1.1 this is density of the algebraic sum of the $\mathcal H_j$. For continuous $f$ and $\varepsilon>0$, choose a finite sum $q$ of harmonic modes with $\|f-q\|_\infty<\varepsilon$. Put $P_{\le N}f=\sum_{\ell=0}^N P_\ell f$ and $V_N=\bigoplus_{\ell=0}^N\mathcal H_\ell$. Orthogonality from step 1.2 makes $f-P_{\le N}f$ orthogonal to $V_N$, so Pythagoras shows $P_{\le N}f$ is a best $L^2$ approximation in $V_N$. For $N$ at least the largest degree in $q$, $\|f-P_{\le N}f\|_2\le\|f-q\|_2\le\sqrt{4\pi}\varepsilon$. Since $\varepsilon$ is arbitrary, the ordered partial sums converge in $L^2$.

For smooth $f$ and $\ell\ge1$, self-adjointness just proved gives $P_\ell(\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}^m f)=(-\ell(\ell+1))^mP_\ell f$. The finite-dimensional projection is a contraction in $L^2$, hence $\|P_\ell f\|_2\le[\ell(\ell+1)]^{-m}\|\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}^m f\|_2$. Taking $m$ arbitrarily large proves the asserted decay (and degree zero is absorbed into $C_m(f)$).

Let $X_1,X_2,X_3$ be the infinitesimal rotation fields on the sphere about the coordinate axes. Rotations preserve $\mathcal H_\ell$ and surface measure, so $X_j$ preserves $\mathcal H_\ell$ and is skew-adjoint. Expanding these three fields in spherical coordinates gives $X_1^2+X_2^2+X_3^2=\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}$. Thus $\sum_j\|X_jg\|_2^2=-\langle\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}g,g\rangle=\ell(\ell+1)\|g\|_2^2$, so each $X_j$ has operator norm at most $\sqrt{\ell(\ell+1)}$ on $\mathcal H_\ell$. Iteration and step 1.3 bound every word of $q$ rotation derivatives pointwise by $\sqrt{(2\ell+1)/(4\pi)}[\ell(\ell+1)]^{q/2}\|g\|_2$. $$j_\ell(z):=(-z)^\ell D_z^\ell\left(\frac{\sin z}{z}\right),\qquad h_\ell^{(1)}(z):=(-z)^\ell D_z^\ell\left(-i\frac{e^{iz}}{z}\right).$$
The definition fixes the outgoing $e^{iz}$ convention. The functions solve the radial Helmholtz equation and have the recurrence, origin, Wronskian, and infinity behavior by [[lem-spherical-bessel-and-hankel-radial-solutions]].

Then $L_\ell j_\ell=L_\ell h_\ell^{(1)}=0$, and for $y=j,h^{(1)}$,
$$y_{\ell+1}(z)=\frac{\ell}{z}y_\ell(z)-y_\ell'(z),\qquad y_\ell'(z)=y_{\ell-1}(z)-\frac{\ell+1}{z}y_\ell(z)\quad(\ell\ge1).$$
The regular-origin and outgoing-infinity normalizations are
$$j_\ell(z)=\frac{z^\ell}{(2\ell+1)!!}+O(z^{\ell+2}),\quad h_\ell^{(1)}(z)=-i(2\ell-1)!!z^{-\ell-1}(1+O(z))\quad(z\downarrow0),$$

$$\lim_{r\to\infty}\sup_{\omega\in\mathbb S^2}\left|r\bigl(\partial_r u(r\omega)-ik u(r\omega)\bigr)\right|=0.$$
The time factor is $e^{-i\omega t}$, so this is the outgoing convention. The obstacle is the closed ball $\{|x|\le a\}$; its boundary is smooth and its exterior is connected. This definition makes no claim for nonspherical obstacles or nonsmooth data.

$$\|g\|_\infty\le\sqrt{\frac{2\ell+1}{4\pi}}\,\|g\|_2.$$
For each integer $p\ge0$ there is $C_p$ independent of $\ell,g$ such that $\|g\|_{C^p(\mathbb S^2)}\le C_p(1+\ell)^{p+1/2}\|g\|_2$.
The angular Dirichlet form satisfies $-\langle\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}g,g\rangle=\ell(\ell+1)\|g\|_2^2$ for $g\in\mathcal H_\ell$.

derivations.claim: Fix $\ell$ and any $v\in\mathcal H_\ell$. Define $w_v(r)=\langle u(r,\cdot),v\rangle_{L^2(\mathbb S^2)}$. Integrating the polar-coordinate Helmholtz equation against $v$, using $\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}v=-\ell(\ell+1)v$ and the angular integration-by-parts identity from [F2], gives $w_v''+2r^{-1}w_v'+(k^2-\ell(\ell+1)r^{-2})w_v=0$. Since this holds for every vector in the finite-dimensional space, the projected vector $u_\ell(r,\cdot)$ solves the same scalar radial equation componentwise.

The two functions $h_\ell^{(1)}(kr)$ and $h_\ell^{(2)}(kr)$ solve this equation and have nonzero Wronskian by [F3]–[F4]; hence at any fixed $r_0>a$ their value-derivative vectors form an invertible $2\times2$ matrix. Solve this matrix equation to match a coefficient and its derivative at $r_0$. The difference then solves a first-order system $Y'=M(r)Y$ with continuous $M$ and zero initial data. On each compact interval where $\|M\|\le C$, integration gives $|Y(r)|\le C\int_{r_0}^r|Y(s)|ds$ (or the reversed integral for $r<r_0$); Grönwall's inequality gives $Y=0$. Extending across compact intervals proves every coefficient is a linear combination of the two modes.

Apply the uniform radiation condition [F1] to any $v\in\mathcal H_\ell$ and integrate it against $\bar v$; its coefficient tends to zero because its magnitude is bounded by the uniform supremum times $\|v\|_{L^1}$. For the outgoing mode, the asymptotic and derivative recurrence in [F3] give $r(\partial_r-ik)h_\ell^{(1)}(kr)\to0$. For the incoming conjugate, the same recurrence gives $r(\partial_r-ik)h_\ell^{(2)}(kr)=-2i\,\overline{(-i)^{\ell+1}}e^{-ikr}+o(1)$, whose magnitude tends to $2$. Thus its coefficient in the mode combination from step 1.2 must vanish. Since this holds for every $v$, the projected vector is $c_\ell h_\ell^{(1)}(kr)$ for a fixed $c_\ell\in\mathcal H_\ell$. The argument treats each degree separately and uses no interchange of the degree sum with the limit $r\to\infty$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $\Gamma$ be a polyhedral boundary as in [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]]. A **conforming surface triangulation** $\mathcal T_h$ is a finite collection of nondegenerate closed planar triangles covering $\Gamma$, with disjoint relative interiors, such that two distinct triangles meet only in a common full edge, a common vertex, or not at all. For $T\in\mathcal T_h$, write $h_T=\operatorname{diam}(T)$ and let $\rho_T$ be the radius of the largest disk contained in $T$; the family is **shape regular** if $\sup_{h,T}h_T/\rho_T<\infty$, and **quasi-uniform** if $\inf_{h,T}h_T/h>0$ for $h=\max_{T\in\mathcal T_h}h_T$.

The conforming **P0 density space** is $X_h=\{\lambda_h\in L^2(\Gamma):\lambda_h|_T\text{ is constant for every }T\in\mathcal T_h\}$. The continuous inclusion $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)\hookrightarrow L^2(\Gamma)$ follows because each chart Bessel norm controls its L2 norm and the fixed partition is finite. Hence every $\lambda_h$ defines a bounded functional $v\mapsto\int_\Gamma\lambda_hv$ on $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$; thus $X_h\subset H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$. This inclusion makes the single-layer Galerkin method conforming in its energy space.

For $x\ne y$ in $\mathbb R^3$, the Newton kernel is $G_3(x,y)=(4\pi|x-y|)^{-1}$. Its distributional fundamental-solution property $-\Delta_xG_3(x,y)=\delta_y$ is proved in [[lem-bem-newtonian-kernel-is-fundamental-solution]]. The kernel fixes the sign and $4\pi$ normalization for every three-dimensional layer operator on this page.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For every $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$, with $\Gamma$ as in [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]], there is a unique $u=S\lambda\in\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ satisfying the weak single-layer equation of [[def-bem-laplace-layer-potentials-and-energy-spaces]]. It is harmonic on $\Omega^-$ and $\Omega^+$, its two traces agree, and its weak conormal traces satisfy
$$\partial_n^-u-\partial_n^+u=\lambda\quad\hbox{in }H^{-1/2}(\Gamma).$$
The trace operator $V\lambda:=\gamma u$ maps $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ boundedly into $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, and there are constants $C,c>0$ depending on $\Gamma$ such that
$$\|u\|_{\dot H^1}+\|V\lambda\|_{H^{1/2}}\le C\|\lambda\|_{H^{-1/2}},\qquad \langle\lambda,V\lambda\rangle_\Gamma\ge c\|\lambda\|_{H^{-1/2}}^2.$$
If $\lambda\in L^\infty(\Gamma)$ (in particular for facewise smooth densities reaching edges or discontinuous P0 densities), this weak potential agrees away from $\Gamma$ with $\int_\Gamma(4\pi|x-y|)^{-1}\lambda(y)dS_y$.

For $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ define the Laplace Calderon boundary operators by
$$V\lambda=\gamma S\lambda,\qquad K\phi=\tfrac12(\gamma^-D\phi+\gamma^+D\phi),$$
$$K'\lambda=\tfrac12(\partial_n^-S\lambda+\partial_n^+S\lambda),\qquad W\phi=-\partial_n^-D\phi=-\partial_n^+D\phi.$$
Here $\gamma S\lambda$ is the common trace, conormal traces use the orientation of [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]], and the last equality is meaningful because the weak double layer has a common conormal derivative. This page uses the real duality pairing between $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$. The well-definedness and bounded mapping properties of $V,K,K',W$ are proved in [[thm-bem-calderon-mapping-and-jump-identities]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice and let $\Gamma$ be any compact Lipschitz boundary in the geometry of [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]]; no polyhedral restriction is imposed. The interior trace $\gamma^-:H^1(\Omega^-)\to H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ is bounded. On every bounded exterior boundary collar $C=\Omega^+\cap U$, where $U$ is a bounded neighborhood of $\Gamma$ with Lipschitz collar boundary, the exterior trace $\gamma^+:H^1(C)\to H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ is bounded. The corresponding localized assertion holds over each boundary chart. Thus an exterior function has this trace whenever it is $H^1$ up to the boundary on such collars; membership in $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega^+)$ alone does not assert a boundary trace. $$\int f\,d\overline{\mu 	imes 
u}=\int_X I_f\,d\mu=\int_Y J_f\,d
u.$$
